reasons: Deviation call is supported: 19.2 gives only 90 days for all Deliverables (playbook fallback, not preferred 12 months for software), and 19.4's refund is tied to "Fees," which Section 1.5 defines as the Implementation Fee alone — a real defect that hollows out the refund leg of the required repair/replace/refund remedy.

Redline is directionally correct and customer-favorable: it extends the period for software Deliverables to twelve (12) months while preserving 90 days for other Deliverables, leaves the already-better Hosted Services subscription-term warranty untouched, and expands the refund to all amounts paid for the non-conforming item.

Rule completeness is satisfied: professional-and-workmanlike and documentation conformity (19.1), Applicable Law and no-malicious-code (19.3), and a disclaimer that expressly preserves the express warranties (19.5) are correctly identified as compliant, so no further operations are required.

Comment is accurate, correctly cites the 12-month/90-day playbook position, explains the "Fees" definitional problem, and offers a sensible alternative (broadening Section 1.5); tone matches house style.

Advisory changed-character ratio on p0080 (0.630) does not indicate over-editing in substance — only the refund phrase within one sentence was touched; the parenthetical "(and not only the Implementation Fee)" is arguably surplus and could be trimmed, and "software Deliverables" is not a defined term given Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology, but neither creates customer risk.
